To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of a mirror affects the resonance interaction energy of two accelerated atoms and, moreover, that the radiation-reaction field contribution to the resonance interaction energy, beyond the Unrah temperature, is not affected by the acceleration of the atoms, but only by the presence of the plate, and that the presence of an accelerated plate affects both the resonance interaction energy and the radiation-reaction energy.

the resonance dipole-dipol interaction between two uniformly accelerated atoms, one excited in the ground state and interacting with a perfectly reflecting plane boundary, is related only to the radiation-reaction field.
the resonant dipolar interaction between two uniformly accelerated atoms, prepared in a Bell-type entangled state, is affected by the presence of a reflecting plane boundary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantum electrodynamical description of a pair of atoms, prepared in a Bell-type state and uniformly accelerated, interacting with the quantum electromagnetic field near a plane boundary.

the study of the resonant dipolar interaction energy between two identical atoms, one of which is in the excited state and the other in its ground state, and interacting through the vacuum fluctuations and the radiation reaction field in the presence of a perfectly reflecting plate, and prepared in a correlated Bell state
the study of quantum vacuum effects of accelerated atoms, and with the investigation of the possible experimental consequences of such effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the Unruh acceleration temperature equivalence is not valid for the resonance dipole-dipoles interaction between two accelerated atoms in the presence of a reflecting plate, it is valid for the resonance interaction between two accelerated and two nonaccelerated atoms in the free-space.

the resonance dipole-dipoles interaction energy between two accelerated atoms in the free-space and in the presence of a reflecting boundary can be used to detect the effects of atomic acceleration, and to distinguish between the different effects of acceleration on radiative process.

the presence of a reflecting plane boundary, together with the peculiar structure of quantum electromagnetic field vacuum, affects the resonance interaction between uniformly accelerated atoms in a nontrivial way, and that these effects are not equivalent to the Unruh thermal effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a reflecting boundary, in a locally inertial frame, modifies the resonance interaction between uniformly accelerated atoms.
, in the presence of an acceleration, the radiation-reaction field of an atom is modified and the interaction between atoms can be affected by the boundary.

the resonant dipolar interaction between two uniformly accelerated atoms is not modified by Unruh thermal effects, but is affected by the acceleration non-thermal effects beyond the Unruh equivalence principle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a mirror, in the case of two uniformly accelerated atoms interacting with the electromagnetic field, may lead to new features and new effects in the resonance energy shift, which can be exploited to probe acceleration effects in the radiation reaction field.

a nonthermal effect of atomic acceleration on the resonance interaction energy, beyond the Unrhun acceleration-temperature equivalence principle, is present and can be detected by measuring the resonance interaction energy in specific configurations of the atoms relative to the plate.
a nontrivial effect on the resonant dipolar interaction between two atoms, due to the presence of a reflecting plane boundary, may be detected by measuring the resonance energy shift.
